question: What is the standard width of a hockey field?
solution:
The correct answer is __**55 meters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **standard width** of a hockey field is **55 meters**, as per the specifications set by the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)**.
 
• The **length of a hockey field** is standardized to **91.4 meters**, making it rectangular in shape with specific proportions.
 
• The field is divided into two halves, with a **centerline** marking the midpoint.
 
• These dimensions are used for **international competitions** and are adhered to in official tournaments globally.
 
• The field also includes distinct markings for the **shooting circle**, penalty spots, and sidelines, which are crucial for gameplay.
 
• The dimensions ensure uniformity and provide a standard structure for **training, matches, and competitions.**
 
• The size of the field is designed to balance **speed, skill, and teamwork**, which are key components of hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Hockey Federation (FIH)**__

 __
 
• The **FIH** is the governing body for field hockey and indoor hockey worldwide.
 
• It was founded in **1924** in Paris, France, and is responsible for setting **rules and standards** for the sport.
 
• The FIH oversees major international tournaments like the **Hockey World Cup** and the **Hockey Pro League**.
 
 
 
• **Hockey Field Markings**__
 __
 
• The **shooting circle** is marked 14.63 meters from the goalpost and is critical for scoring.
 
• The field includes a **penalty spot** located 6.4 meters from the goal line, used for penalty strokes.
 
• Sidelines and backlines ensure that the boundaries of the game are clearly defined for fair play.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Standard Dimensions**__
 
 
• Standardized dimensions ensure a **level playing field** for all teams and players worldwide.
 
• They help in maintaining consistency in **training and competitive matches.**
 
• These dimensions are also critical for constructing **hockey fields** that comply with international standards.
